question: The constellation which one can see during the early part of a summer night is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ursa Major**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ursa Major** is a prominent constellation visible in the northern hemisphere.
 
• It is most easily seen in the spring and early summer evenings.
 
• Ursa Major is known for its distinctive pattern often referred to as the "Big Dipper".
 
• The constellation is one of the largest and most recognizable in the night sky.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cassiopeia**

 
 
• Cassiopeia is a constellation in the northern sky named after the vain queen Cassiopeia in Greek mythology.
 
• It is easily recognizable due to its distinctive 'W' shape formed by five bright stars.
 
• It is best seen in the autumn and winter months in the northern hemisphere.
 
 
 
• **Orion**
 
 
• Orion is a prominent constellation located on the celestial equator and visible throughout the world.
 
• It is best seen during the winter months in the northern hemisphere.
 
• Orion is known for its bright stars, including Betelgeuse and Rigel, and its distinctive "belt" of three stars.
 
 
 
• **Leo Major**
 
 
• Leo Major, often simply referred to as Leo, is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
 
• It is visible in the evening sky during the spring and early summer months.
 
• Leo is known for its bright star Regulus and its distinctive shape that resembles a lion.
